title: Range Managers
description: Research or study range land management practices to provide sustained production of forage, livestock, and wildlife.

tasks.text: Manage forage resources through fire, herbicide use, or revegetation to maintain a sustainable yield from the land.
Maintain soil stability and vegetation for non-grazing uses, such as wildlife habitats and outdoor recreation.
Tailor conservation plans to landowners' goals, such as livestock support, wildlife, or recreation.
Develop technical standards and specifications used to manage, protect, and improve the natural resources of range lands and related grazing lands.
Plan and implement revegetation of disturbed sites.
Study grazing patterns to determine number and kind of livestock that can be most profitably grazed and to determine the best grazing seasons.
Study rangeland management practices and research range problems to provide sustained production of forage, livestock, and wildlife.
Study forage plants and their growth requirements to determine varieties best suited to particular range.

Regulate grazing, such as by issuing permits and checking for compliance with standards, and help ranchers plan and organize grazing systems to manage, improve, protect, and maximize the use of rangelands.
Measure and assess vegetation resources for biological assessment companies, environmental impact statements, and rangeland monitoring programs.

clusters.label: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

tasks.text: Develop methods for protecting range from fire and rodent damage and for controlling poisonous plants.
Develop new and improved instruments and techniques for activities, such as range reseeding.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Coordinate with federal land managers and other agencies and organizations to manage and protect rangelands.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Offer advice to rangeland users on water management, forage production methods, and control of brush.
Plan and direct construction and maintenance of range improvements, such as fencing, corrals, stock-watering reservoirs, and soil-erosion control structures.

clusters.label: Resolving Conflicts and Negotiating with Others

tasks.text: Mediate agreements among rangeland users and preservationists as to appropriate land use and management.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Writing

skills.name: Active Learning

skills.name: Negotiation

skills.name: Systems Analysis

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: Oracle Java, Perl, Python, R.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Linux, Microsoft Windows, UNIX.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: Aquatic Plant Information Retrieval System APIRS, Automated Geospatial Watershed Assessment AGWA, BehavePlus, Clark Labs IDRISI Selva.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Microsoft Access, National Resources Conservation Service Ecological Site Information System ESIS, National Resources Conservation Service Web Soil Survey WSS, Satellite image databases.

skills.name: Geographic information system
skills.def: Software to capture, manage, analyze, or display geographically-referenced information. Examples: ESRI ArcGIS software, ESRI software, Geographic information system GIS systems.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Photoshop, GNU Image Manipulation Program GIMP.
